GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2018-10-26T18:43:03Z

Title: Virtual fields that rely on sibling fields
Description: <!--

Please note this is an issue tracker, not a support forum.
For general questions, please use StackOverflow or Slack.

For bugs, please fill out the template below.

-->

## What are you doing?

When you have a model with virtual fields that rely on other fields then you exclude that field in a query, your custom getter doesn't work. Is this a feature that should be added? Or is there a better pattern I should be using?

```js
module.exports = function (sequelize,DataTypes) {
  var Widget = sequelize.define('Widget',{
    data: {
      type: DataTypes.TEXT
    },
    info: {
      type: DataTypes.VIRTUAL,
      get: function () {
        return JSON.parse(this.data).info;
      }
    }
  });
};
```

Excluding the `data` field would break the query.

## What do you expect to happen?

Wanted my virtual field tow work

## What is actually happening?

My virtual field doesn't work when the requisite sibling fields are excluded from the query.

__Dialect:__ sqlite
__Dialect version:__
__Database version:__
__Sequelize version:__ 4.41.0
__Tested with latest release:__

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about a conceptual problem with Sequelize's virtual fields and how they interact with field exclusion in queries. The user has a virtual field "info" that depends on the "data" field, but when "data" is excluded from a query, the virtual field doesn't work. This is a logical behavior issue that can be analyzed without needing to build or run the code. The solution would involve either ensuring the dependent field is always included in queries or restructuring the model. This can be verified through code analysis and understanding of how Sequelize's virtual fields work, without needing to set up a build environment.
